channel.title: Psycholopedia (English)
channel.description: Three psychology articles every three days.

item.title: The Stroop effect: when reading outruns looking
item.description: A simple task, naming the colour of the ink, published in 1935, has become one of the most robust findings in psychology.

item.title: Do opposites attract?
item.description: It is a favourite of films and songs, but research on attraction and couples nearly always points the other way.

item.title: Black Friday: what psychology knows about the buying mind
item.description: Scarcity, countdowns and crossed-out prices. Some well-studied mechanisms that explain why we buy more than we meant to, and how to pause in time.

item.title: How the first intelligence test was born
item.description: Alfred Binet created it to help children who were falling behind at school. It was soon used for purposes he would not have approved of.

item.title: Mary Ainsworth and the 'Strange Situation'
item.description: Twenty minutes of observation in a playroom changed how we understand the bond between babies and those who care for them.

item.title: Teenage sleep is not laziness
item.description: Why teenagers find it hard to fall asleep early and get up early, and what can help at home.

item.title: When psychology put itself to the test
item.description: In 2015, hundreds of researchers repeated a hundred published studies. The result shook the discipline and has made it more rigorous.

item.title: Neuromyths in the classroom
item.description: Learning styles, left and right brain, the 10% of the brain… Many teachers believe ideas that research does not support.

item.title: What we know (and don't) about gratitude
item.description: Writing down what we are grateful for has become fashionable. Studies show real effects, but more modest than some books promise.

item.title: Unwanted loneliness is a health matter too
item.description: Being alone and feeling lonely are not the same. What research says and what each of us can do.

item.title: Cajal and the 'butterflies of the soul'
item.description: How a doctor from Aragon, drawing at the microscope, showed that the brain is made of separate cells.

item.title: The holidays are not always happy
item.description: The holidays bring joy to many, and nostalgia, stress or loneliness to others. What is true in the clichés and what can help.

item.title: Understand the mind, understand life: introducing Psycholopedia
item.description: Why an encyclopedia of psychology that links the discipline's history with everyday questions.

item.title: Shorter days: light, sleep and mood in autumn
item.description: With fewer hours of daylight, many people feel sleepier and less energetic. What is normal and when to seek advice.

item.title: Ebbinghaus, the man who tested himself
item.description: How a German researcher measured forgetting with nonsense syllables, and why his curve still holds.
